answer: Roll-call challenges hash a round whisper digest, each identity’s shale-sealed key history, and its nectar bond into a fresh prompt; a sampled quorum checks for a live, identity-specific answer, rejecting replayed or shared replies. Attackers pay one bond per identity, a per-attempt fee, clear five cross-checkers, and wait out a rate-capped trust window. A coordinated ring fails because answers bind to separate histories, so copied replies break distinctness and shared bonds expose collusion.
